Evan / Julia —

Appreciate the MAP — looks clear. High-level sequencing I recommend below (I'll put a simple two-column table into a shared sheet and send link). TL;DR: we can enable sandbox provisioning before signed MSA if you sign an interim NDA + pilot order form; production capacity requires MSA + DPA signed.

Proposed sequencing (short):
1) Exchange NDA (if needed) — 1–2 business days
2) Pilot order form (POF) signed — enables sandbox credentials and limited usage; we can start ingestion and eval work.
3) DPA review in parallel with POF — typical turnaround 5–7 business days for standard redlines; may extend if customer-side legal requests bespoke logging/retention terms.
4) MSA redlines — parallel loop with DPA; MSA should be agreed before full production provisioning (target 10–15 business days depending on redlines).
5) Final order form amendment to add production capacity and SLA terms — after MSA executed.

Risks and notes:
- If Novamedix requires unusual data residency or an on-prem deployment, DPA/MSA review steps lengthen.
- SOC 2 evidence we can share immediately; Karthik, can you confirm which artifacts (audit report + security questionnaire) we should push first?

Next actions:
- Karthik: quick scan for any immediate MSA red flags and confirm evidence bundle 
- Ben: I'll sync with infra to confirm earliest sandbox provisioning date if we get a signed POF this week
- Evan/Julia: can you confirm whether your procurement team needs a PO number ahead of the POF?

I'll upload a simple sequencing sheet and a proposed calendar (I moved tentative dates around the MAP to reflect the pilot-week Oct 18 start).

Best,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Rachel / team —

Quick read of the MAP and the MSA excerpt Evan shared. High-level legal stance and gating items:
- DPA: confirm role/role-based language (controller/processor) and retention limits. If Novamedix needs contractually guaranteed deletion timelines shorter than our standard 90 days, expect an extra review.
- Security Addendum: provide SOC 2 Type II report + security questionnaire (we can send the doc bundle today).
- IP: keep standard Redwood IP carve-outs; Novamedix-specific IP claims for model outputs need to be scoped in the order form.
- Liability/SLA: Novamedix asks for a 99.9% SLA? We'll propose a Tiered SLA in the order form (pilot non-production: best-effort; production: SLA tied to dedicated capacity purchase).

Suggested gating checklist for legal/procurement sequencing (short bullets):
- Step A: Sign POF (sandbox) + NDA if missing — Redwood provides access credentials and security bundle.
- Step B: DPA in parallel — target 5 business days if no custom retention or residency asks.
- Step C: MSA redline loop — expect 10 business days if standard redlines; add buffer for procurement.
- Step D: Finalize production order form and SLA appendices — 3 business days after MSA.

I'll attach a redlines PDF with comments (MSA_redlines_v3.pdf) and a short checklist we use internally. Rachel — once Ben confirms provisioning lead times, we can publish a calendar to the MAP sheet.

Karthik Iyer
Lead, Legal Contracts (Redwood Inference)
